sample_unit: test text instances from psychiatric hospital clinical notes

links.outcome: Character-level precision, recall and F1 of PII removal versus alternative de-identification systems
links.effect: Fine-tuned GLiNER micro-average F1 0.980 vs Gemini-Pro-2.5 0.845; 95% of documents fully sanitised vs 64% for next-best; 2% entity-level false negative rate remained.
links.quote: The fine-tuned GLiNER model achieved superior performance, with an overall micro-average F1-score of 0.980, significantly outperforming Gemini-Pro-2.5 (F1-score: 0.845).

unlisted_practices: Locally deployable lightweight fine-tuned NER model for PII removal at the source without sending data to external APIs
Human-in-the-loop validation of automated de-identification output

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks a specialized lightweight NER model (GLiNER-based) against LLMs and other de-identification tools for removing PII from clinical text. Developing and evaluating a new model's de-identification performance without testing organizational deployment practices is categorized as benchmark_only and tests_practice is false.
